title: Part 4 Practice: Ties That Connect: Marriage

questions.text: Why is it difficult to have a single universally applicable definition of marriage?
options: A) Because marriage is the same in all cultures.
B) Because of cross-cultural variability and the existence of rare forms of marriage (e.g., Nuer woman marriage, fraternal polyandry).
C) Because marriage is only defined by law.
D) Because marriage does not exist in some cultures.
questions.correct_answer: B) Because of cross-cultural variability and the existence of rare forms of marriage (e.g., Nuer woman marriage, fraternal polyandry).
questions.explanation: The module states: 'There is no one universally applicable definition of marriage, because of the Cross-Cultural Variability in the existence of rare forms of marriage in specific societies.'

questions.text: What is the rule of exogamy?
options: A) A rule requiring individuals to marry within their own group.
B) A rule prohibiting marriage with someone from one's own social group, often considered incest.
C) A rule allowing marriage with any relative.
D) A rule requiring marriage with a specific cousin.
questions.correct_answer: B) A rule prohibiting marriage with someone from one's own social group, often considered incest.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Exogamy: This is the rule by which a man is not allowed to marry someone from his own social group. Such a prohibited union is designated as incest.'

questions.text: What is the primary adaptive value of exogamy according to Kottak?
options: A) It keeps wealth within the family.
B) It links people into a wider social network, establishing alliances and providing protection.
C) It prevents all marriage.
D) It ensures everyone marries a relative.
questions.correct_answer: B) It links people into a wider social network, establishing alliances and providing protection.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Kottak claimed also that exogamy has adaptive value, because it links people into a wider social network that nurtures, helps, and protects them in times of need pushing social organization outward, establishing and preserving alliances among groups.'

questions.text: What is the rule of endogamy?
options: A) A rule requiring individuals to marry within their own group.
B) A rule requiring marriage outside the group.
C) A rule allowing marriage with any relative.
D) A rule against marriage.
questions.correct_answer: A) A rule requiring individuals to marry within their own group.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A rule of endogamy requires individuals to marry within their own group and forbids them to marry outside it.'

questions.text: What is the difference between cross cousins and parallel cousins?
options: A) Cross cousins are children of siblings of the opposite sex; parallel cousins are children of siblings of the same sex.
B) They are the same.
C) Cross cousins are the same as parallel cousins.
D) Cross cousins are siblings of the same sex; parallel cousins are siblings of the opposite sex.
questions.correct_answer: A) Cross cousins are children of siblings of the opposite sex; parallel cousins are children of siblings of the same sex.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Cross Cousins: are children of siblings of the opposite sex... Parallel Cousins: When marriage takes place between the children of the siblings of the same sex, it is called parallel cousin marriage.'

options: A) A widower marries the sister of his deceased wife.
B) A widow is expected to marry the brother of her dead husband.
C) A woman marries multiple men.
D) A man marries multiple women.
questions.correct_answer: B) A widow is expected to marry the brother of her dead husband.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The levirate- is the custom whereby a widow is expected to marry the brother (or some close male relative) of her dead husband.'

C) A man marries multiple women.
D) A woman marries multiple men.
questions.correct_answer: A) A widower marries the sister of his deceased wife.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The sororate, which comes into play when a wife dies, is the practice of a widower's marrying the sister (or some close female relative) of his deceased wife.'

questions.text: What is the most common form of polygamy?
options: A) Polyandry.
B) Polygyny.
C) Monogamy.
D) Serial monogamy.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Polygyny is much more common.'

options: A) Payment from the bride's family to the groom's family.
B) Compensation given by the family of the groom to the family of the bride upon marriage.
C) A gift exchanged equally between families.
D) The labor a groom provides to the bride's family.
questions.correct_answer: B) Compensation given by the family of the groom to the family of the bride upon marriage.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Bride wealth: It is the compensation given upon marriage by the family of the groom to the family of the bride.'

questions.text: What does dowry correlate with according to the module?
options: A) Higher female status.
B) Lower female status, as women are perceived as burdens.
C) Equal status.
D) No correlation.
questions.correct_answer: B) Lower female status, as women are perceived as burdens.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Dowry, best known in India but also practiced in Europe, correlates with lower female status. Women are perceived as burdens.'
